skill.name: doc-coauthoring
skill.description: Structured workflow for co-authoring documentation, proposals, specs, RFCs, and decision docs through context gathering, iterative drafting, and reader testing.
skill.summary: Guides collaborative document drafting from context gathering through reader validation.
skill.author: Azeem-2

content.value_statement: Writing complex docs is hard when context, structure, and reader assumptions are unclear. This skill guides context capture, section drafting, iterative edits, and reader testing.
actual_capabilities: Guides users through context gathering before drafting.
Builds document structures with placeholders for each section.
Drafts sections through questions, brainstorming, curation, and targeted edits.
Supports proposals, technical specs, RFCs, PRDs, and decision docs.
Tests drafts with a fresh Claude or sub-agent perspective.
Checks completed docs for flow, gaps, contradictions, and generic filler.
limitations: Requires the user to provide or authorize access to source context.
Does not verify facts, links, or technical details without additional review.
May not access Slack, Teams, Drive, or SharePoint unless connectors are configured.
Uses iterative drafting, so it is slower than simple freeform writing.

use_cases.title: Draft a Technical Spec
use_cases.description: Turn architecture notes, constraints, and tradeoffs into a structured spec that reviewers can understand.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Decision Document
use_cases.description: Compare options, capture reasoning, and refine the recommendation before stakeholders review it.

use_cases.title: Validate Docs Before Sharing
use_cases.description: Use reader testing to find gaps, ambiguity, and hidden assumptions before publishing a document.

prompt_templates.title: Start a New Doc
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the doc-coauthoring workflow to help me draft a [document type] for [audience]. Start by asking the initial context questions.

prompt_templates.title: Build from Notes
prompt_templates.prompt: I have rough notes for a [proposal/spec/decision doc]. Help me organize them into sections, then draft one section at a time.

prompt_templates.title: Refine an Existing Draft
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my draft for flow, redundancy, missing context, and unclear assumptions. Suggest targeted edits instead of rewriting the whole document.

prompt_templates.title: Run Reader Testing
prompt_templates.prompt: Act as a fresh reader for this document. Predict likely reader questions, test whether the draft answers them, and list gaps to fix.

output_examples.input: I need an RFC about replacing our deployment pipeline.
output: Initial questions about audience, constraints, and desired impact.
A plan to draft and refine the technical approach first.

output_examples.input: Here is my decision doc draft. Please make it clearer.
output: A review of flow, redundancy, contradictions, and missing context.
A reader testing checklist for final validation.

output_examples.input: Help me test whether this proposal works for executives.
output: Recommended fixes for sections that need clearer context.

best_practices: Provide audience, impact, constraints, and source context before drafting.
Work section by section and give specific feedback after each draft.
Run reader testing before sharing the document with stakeholders.
anti_patterns: Starting with a polished draft before the problem and audience are clear.
Asking for full-document rewrites when targeted edits would preserve style.
Skipping final fact checks for links, dates, metrics, and technical claims.

faq.question: What document types does this skill support?
faq.answer: It supports proposals, technical specs, RFCs, PRDs, decision docs, and similar structured documents.

faq.question: Does it write the whole document at once?
faq.answer: No. It builds the document section by section so each part can be reviewed and improved.

faq.question: Can it use existing templates?
faq.answer: Yes. Provide the template as a file, link, or pasted content before the structure is created.

faq.question: Can it read team channels or shared docs?
faq.answer: Only if the required connectors or integrations are available and the user authorizes access.

faq.question: What is reader testing?
faq.answer: Reader testing checks whether a fresh Claude or sub-agent can understand the draft without prior context.

faq.question: Does it replace human review?
faq.answer: No. Users should still verify facts, links, technical claims, and stakeholder expectations before publishing.
